multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Simon's unspoken inner judgment, explicitly framed by 'Simon thought it, not out loud'.

multi_voice_candidates.line_excerpt: When they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both
multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Jesus telling the debtor parable to Simon.

multi_voice_candidates.line_excerpt: Which of them will love him most?
multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Jesus's question closing the parable, same speech as the line before it.

multi_voice_candidates.line_excerpt: I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most.
multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Simon's hedged reply, explicitly framed by 'Simon hedged'.
Jesus turning to address Simon about the woman.

multi_voice_candidates.line_excerpt: Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Continuation of Jesus's same speech to Simon, separated only by a narrator aside.

multi_voice_candidates.line_excerpt: Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
multi_voice_candidates.rationale: Jesus's closing declaration spoken directly to the woman.

concerns: 'Simon thought it, not out loud:' is immediately followed by a quoted line — an auto-tagger keying only on colon+quote may mis-tag this as spoken dialogue rather than unvoiced inner thought; the emotion/delivery tag should reflect silent thought, not speech.

Paragraph 3 has three speaker changes in one paragraph (narrator -> simon (unspoken) -> narrator -> jesus (parable) -> simon (reply)) -- tagger needs to track mid-paragraph speaker switches, not assume one speaker per paragraph.
Ellipses inside several KJV quotes mark elided clauses, not a trailing pause -- do not render them as a spoken pause/trail-off.
The woman never speaks and has no voice entry in the roster; all lines describing her actions stay in narrator voice by design, not an omission.
